text:
[HSTU-BLaIR (2025)](https://kdd2025llm4ecommerce.github.io/assets/accepted/13_HSTU_BLaIR_Lightweight_Cont.pdf) is the closest direct precedent: projected text embeddings are added to item-ID embeddings before HSTU, with text also incorporated into sampled candidate representations. However, it uses fixed embeddings from a pretrained 125M-parameter BLaIR model trained on reviews and metadata—unsuitable for this task’s external-weight and review restrictions. It supports investigating content-enriched HSTU, but does not establish scratch-trained compositional encoding.

[MARS (CIKM 2024)](https://arxiv.org/html/2409.00702v2) motivates preserving multiple attribute representations and learning attribute-wise user–item interactions instead of compressing everything into one pooled vector. Its actual implementation relies on pretrained language models and additional metadata fields. [JEPA4Rec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.10512v2) explores bidirectional item-text encoding and masked representation prediction; reduced pretraining-data requirements should not be interpreted as evidence that external language knowledge is unnecessary. Neither establishes the requested scratch-trained HSTU design; no verified 2026 exact match emerged in this search.

An actionable hypothesis, rather than a published result: retain HSTU and jointly train a small, position-aware text encoder using only permitted titles/descriptions. Character/subword embeddings plus narrow convolutions or shallow attention could represent model identifiers, dimensions and local phrases. Tie the resulting item representation across history inputs, positive targets and negative candidates; combine text and ID features through a jointly learned gate inside the same network. ID-feature dropout could encourage content use for sparse items. Evaluate against unordered pooling under the fixed validation protocol; cold-item gains and phrase sensitivity remain unproven.
